_comment: Curated CAPN3 and DMD evidence bundles (Milestones 1 and 4). CAPN3_c.550del is grounded in a real ClinVar entry (coordinates not independently verified — see notes); all other cases are synthetic, constructed to exercise specific combining-rule paths and, from Milestone 4 on, case-level trans/cis/hemizygous interpretation. Expected results live separately in validation/golden_cases/variant_golden_cases.yaml (variant-level) and case_interpretation_golden_cases.yaml (case-level).

gene_disease_context.disease: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, type R1 calpain3-related (LGMDR1 / calpainopathy)

specification.version: ClinGen LGMD VCEP Specifications to the ACMG/AMP Guidelines for CAPN3, v2.0 (2025-07-09; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21434844)

cases.notes: Real ClinVar entry (Variation ID 17621), reported Pathogenic. Known founder mutation, reported to account for up to ~75% of abnormal CAPN3 alleles in some European (esp. Northern Spanish / Basque and other Southern/Western European) populations — this is why ancestry_specific_max_af is meaningfully higher than overall_af rather than roughly equal. PM2 (absent/extremely low frequency) is written up here as MET in the golden case using the low overall AF (0.023%), but a curator reviewing this case should not treat that as settled: PM2 is defined around population rarity, and a founder allele that is locally common in the tested individual's ancestry group is a weaker fit for 'extremely low frequency' than the global AF alone suggests. This is exactly the ancestry-stratification nuance the ACMG Engine Detailed Design Guide flags for PM2 (Section 7, 'Population frequency thresholds'); a real evaluator should key its threshold check off ancestry_specific_max_af, not overall_af, once ancestry is known. Flagged for manual review in the golden case rather than silently trusted. Exact GRCh38 coordinates were not independently verified during curation (see variant.coordinate_verified=false); HGVS (c.550del) and the ClinVar accession are used as the authoritative identifiers instead.

functional_evidence.assay_description: Western blot calpain-3 protein expression in patient skeletal muscle biopsy
functional_evidence.notes: Real literature functional data for this founder LGMDR1 allele: a Czech cohort study of CAPN3-related LGMD patients (Krahn et al./Chrobakova et al. 2004, Neuromuscul Disord; Hermanova et al. 2006, Muscle Nerve -- Western blot survey of Czech calpainopathy patients) reported total or near-total absence of calpain-3 protein on Western blot in patients carrying c.550delA (legacy nomenclature; equivalent to c.550del/p.Thr184fs here), consistent with a null/frameshift-driven loss of the 94 kDa full-length protein. validation_strength is set to SUPPORTING rather than a higher tier as a DISCLOSED CONSERVATIVE CHOICE: the primary papers were not independently fetchable during curation (PubMed/PMC pages reCAPTCHA-blocked), so the exact number and mix of pathogenic/benign validation controls used in that assay -- which per Brnich et al. 2019's framework is what actually sets Moderate vs. Strong -- could not be verified. SUPPORTING is the safe floor for 'an assay with controls and replicates, documented tier not otherwise confirmable,' not a claim that a higher tier is unwarranted. Western blot for total absence of a frameshift/null allele's protein is also a mechanistically unsurprising, low-ambiguity result (unlike CAPN3_c.2257G>A's missense case below) -- but this project does not use assay type/mechanism alone to justify a higher strength than the validation record can support.

gene_disease_context.disease: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, type R1 calpain3-related (LGMDR1 / calpainopathy)

specification.version: ClinGen LGMD VCEP Specifications to the ACMG/AMP Guidelines for CAPN3, v2.0 (2025-07-09; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21434844)

cases.notes: Real, recurrent CAPN3 missense variant (p.Asp753Asn, ClinVar VCV000281081.42, rs146923842, ClinGen CAID CA7511784), reported in multiple LGMD cohorts (e.g. an 8-patient Italian multicenter series) with real, documented, and now well-sourced controversy. Coordinates (GRCh38 chr15:42410660 G>A, canonical SPDI NC_000015.10:42410659:G:A) confirmed directly from the primary ClinVar VCV page in batch 10, upgrading coordinate_verified from false to true. PRIMARY-SOURCE-CONFIRMED VCEP classification (batch 8 had this secondhand from a web search summary; batch 10 fetched the primary ClinVar page directly and confirmed it verbatim): the ClinGen LGMD VCEP's official 3-star 'reviewed by expert panel' record (SCV007328786.1, evaluated 2025-10-28, erepo.clinicalgenome.org/evrepo/ui/interpretation/8afff73c-4e6c-4e68-9e24-e2192b0159d4) classifies this variant LIKELY BENIGN for autosomal recessive LGMD, via BS1 + BP2. Their exact stated rationale: gnomAD v4.1.0 Grpmax filtering allele frequency 0.002457 (lower 95% CI bound of 22/6060 Middle Eastern chromosomes, including 2 homozygotes) clears their BS1 threshold (>0.001); PM3/PP4 not met (several reported carriers had a second CAPN3 variant that could independently explain their phenotype); one individual's variant was confirmed in cis with a pathogenic variant (c.1401_1403del p.(Glu467del), PMID 38391941) -- BP2; REVEL 0.649, below their PP3 threshold (>=0.70). This project's engine reaches PM2 NOT_MET, BS1 MET (Strong, matching the VCEP), PP3/BP4 both NOT_MET (REVEL genuinely INDETERMINATE by the calibrated-score model used here), landing on VUS -- it cannot reproduce the VCEP's LIKELY_BENIGN call because BP2 (in trans/cis with a pathogenic variant) is not implemented at all, and BS1 alone is Table-5-insufficient for LIKELY_BENIGN without a Supporting-benign criterion alongside it. NEW IN BATCH 10 -- a genuinely opposing real-world signal, not just an unimplemented criterion: a peer-reviewed paper published one month after the VCEP's own evaluation (Bruno et al., 'Recurrent CAPN3 p.Asp753Asn Variant Supports a Potential Dominant Calpainopathy with Variable Clinical Expressivity', Int J Mol Sci 2025;26(23):11384, PMID 41373542, DOI 10.3390/ijms262311384) reports a retrospective multicenter Italian cohort (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05956132) of 59 patients heterozygous for CAPN3 variants, in which p.Asp753Asn was the single most frequent variant found (8 of 59 patients, 13.5%), all heterozygous with NO second CAPN3 variant identified. These 8 patients (aged 6-80) showed a real, if heterogeneous, phenotypic spectrum -- from asymptomatic hyperCKemia to progressive proximal weakness with contractures and axial involvement -- and new structural modeling proposes a specific mechanism (loss of a stabilizing Asp753-Lys517 salt bridge, disrupting inter-domain coupling) consistent with a dominant-negative effect. The paper's own conclusion: 'the aggregated evidence supports a pathogenic role for p.Asp753Asn' -- for a DIFFERENT disease model than the one the VCEP evaluated. The VCEP's Likely Benign call is explicitly scoped to 'autosomal recessive limb girdle muscular dystrophy' (per its own classification comment); this paper is arguing for pathogenicity in autosomal DOMINANT calpainopathy (LGMDD4), a distinct, less common inheritance model for the same gene that the VCEP specification does not appear to address for this variant. These two real, contemporaneous, credentialed sources are not actually contradicting each other on the facts (both cite essentially the same gnomAD frequency and the same REVEL score) -- they are answering different questions (is this pathogenic FOR RECESSIVE disease vs. is this pathogenic FOR DOMINANT disease) that this project's one-inheritance-pattern-per-gene design (gene_disease_context.yaml fixes CAPN3 as AUTOSOMAL_RECESSIVE, full stop) cannot represent at all -- not a gap in any single evaluator, but a gap in the schema itself, previously only mentioned here in passing (batch 8) as a forward-looking note and now fully primary-source-documented. This project's VUS result is, in that light, arguably the most defensible of the three outcomes on offer (VCEP Likely Benign for recessive disease; this paper's suggestive Pathogenic-leaning case for dominant disease; this project's VUS) precisely because it commits to neither disease model and flags the ambiguity instead -- though that is a fortunate byproduct of missing criteria, not a deliberate design strength.

functional_evidence.assay_description: Western blot calpain-3 protein expression in patient skeletal muscle biopsy
functional_evidence.notes: Real, directly-relevant functional data for THIS EXACT variant (p.Asp753Asn), from the same 2025 paper already cited above (Bruno et al., Int J Mol Sci 2025;26(23):11384, PMID 41373542, DOI 10.3390/ijms262311384). Table 1 of that paper reports Western blot results for the 8 heterozygous p.Asp753Asn patients: of 5 with WB performed, calpain-3 expression was Normal in 3 patients and variably Reduced in 2 -- an explicitly mixed, non-discriminating result, not a clean Normal or Abnormal call. The paper states this directly: 'WB analysis of calpain-3 performed in five specimens showed a normal expression of the protein in three patients... while in the other two calpain-3 expression was variably reduced,' and separately cautions that 'approximately 20% of individuals with pathogenic CAPN3 variants may have normal protein levels despite functional impairment' -- i.e. even a Normal WB result cannot safely be read as BS3 for this gene. assay_result is curated as INDETERMINATE (not NORMAL, not ABNORMAL, and no validation_strength) precisely because the source itself concludes the assay does not discriminate for this variant -- this is the real-world illustration the Brnich et al. 2019 framework's INDETERMINATE-outcome caveat exists to cover, not a curation shortfall. Deliberately paired in this fixture set with CAPN3_c.550del's clean ABNORMAL/SUPPORTING result as a contrast case for evaluate_ps3/evaluate_bs3's three-way branch.

cases.notes: Real ClinVar entry (Variation ID 21036, RCV000020097), reported Pathogenic, canonical splice acceptor variant in intron 6. Reported absent from ExAC/gnomAD. Experimental splicing studies (per ClinVar submitter evidence) confirm this variant disrupts mRNA splicing -- real, strong evidence for pathogenicity that this project's PVS1 evaluator cannot use, since it only auto-resolves frameshift/nonsense NMD cases; splice variants are deliberately routed to MANUAL_REVIEW (see pvs1.py). This fixture exists specifically to show that limitation on a real, well-documented pathogenic variant, not just a hypothetical one: our 6-criterion engine lands on VUS here (PM2 MET alone is insufficient per Table 5) despite this being a confidently Pathogenic variant in ClinVar with experimental support. UPDATED in batch 26: the real ClinVar submitter comment cites 'Experimental studies have shown that this variant disrupts mRNA splicing (PMID: 7720071)' -- a real RNA-level study exists for this variant, not just a computational canonical-splice-site prediction. But the available secondary source (the ClinVar submission comment) does not state the resulting transcript's frame or NMD status -- whether the confirmed splicing disruption produces an out-of-frame, NMD-triggering product (which would clear the new CONFIRMED_NULL_EQUIVALENT bar) or something milder is not stated precisely enough to curate safely. splicing_rna_evidence is therefore curated as INCONCLUSIVE, not left unset -- an honest, distinct curation from 'no experimental data at all,' and PVS1 remains MANUAL_REVIEW either way (INCONCLUSIVE routes to the same status as unset), but now with a rationale that correctly reflects a real study exists rather than implying none was ever performed. The original 1995 CAPN3 discovery paper (Richard et al., Cell, PMID 7720071) is the cited source and was not independently re-fetched this batch (paywalled/not readily accessible); the frame/NMD detail may exist in that primary text but couldn't be confirmed from the available secondary source.

gene_disease_context.disease: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, type R1 calpain3-related (LGMDR1 / calpainopathy)

specification.version: ClinGen LGMD VCEP Specifications to the ACMG/AMP Guidelines for CAPN3, v2.0 (2025-07-09; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21434844)

cases.notes: UPDATED this round: when this fixture was added, ClinVar's aggregate call was Uncertain Significance and no computational evidence had been gathered. Re-checked while researching real PS1/PM5 fixtures (this batch) and found the real ClinGen LGMD VCEP itself reclassified this variant Pathogenic on 2026-01-20 (ClinVar VCV000217149, RCV006646441.1, reviewed by expert panel, 3-star; accession SCV007540248.1), via PM3_Strong (in trans with c.550del, c.1319G>A p.(Arg440Gln), c.2362_2363delinsTCATCT p.(Arg788SerfsTer14), and c.2120A>G p.(Asp707Gly) across multiple case reports), PP4_Strong (a patient with two diagnostic CAPN3 alleles including this one had absent calpain-3 protein on muscle biopsy), PM2_Supporting (Grpmax AF 0.00000263, Admixed American, 1/58530 chromosomes gnomAD v4.1.0 -- matches this fixture's pre-existing overall_af almost exactly), and PP3 (REVEL 0.904, above the VCEP's >=0.70 threshold -- now added here as this fixture's computational_evidence, closing the gap the original notes disclosed). Coordinates (GRCh38 chr15:42399641 G>A) confirmed directly from the primary ClinVar page; coordinate_verified upgraded from false to true. This project's 6-criterion engine only implements PM2 and PP3 of the VCEP's four applied criteria -- PM3 and PP4 are case-level/segregation criteria this project's variant-only design does not reach (see clinical.py's own scope notes on why PM3 in particular cannot be a per-variant evaluator). PM2 Supporting + PP3 Supporting alone does not clear any Table 5 pathogenic-tier rule (no rule for '2 Supporting' without a Moderate or Strong alongside), so this project's engine still lands on VUS -- a fifth independent confirmation of batch 13's structural finding (no real CAPN3 variant reaches Pathogenic/Likely Pathogenic through this engine), now shown even with a criterion (PP3) added after the original VUS call. PS1/PM5 note: a real, different-amino-acid-change precedent now exists at this exact residue (c.1342C>T p.(Arg448Cys), ClinVar VCV000280038, also reclassified Pathogenic by the same LGMD VCEP on the same date -- see that fixture) that could in principle support PM5 for THIS variant too (PM5 is symmetric: each missense change at a residue can cite the other as precedent). The real VCEP's own published rationale for this variant does not list PM5 among its applied criteria, even though it explicitly invoked PM5 in the other direction (citing this exact variant as p.Arg448Cys's precedent). The likely reason, per the VCEP's own general PM5 specification text ('PM5 can potentially be applied to multiple amino acid changes at the same residue as long as the variant classification that determines the strength level does not depend on PM5 application'), is that both variants were curated and classified on the same date (2026-01-20) using PM3_Strong/PP4_Strong alone, sufficient without PM5 -- applying it mutually in both directions from a single joint curation event risks the same kind of circularity this project's own clinical.py docstring already flags for PM3. Rather than invent an answer to that open question, this fixture deliberately leaves same_residue_evidence unset (not pm5_precedent_established=True) -- mirroring the real VCEP's own choice not to invoke it here, an honest 'not curated one way or the other' rather than a guess in either direction.

cases.notes: Real CAPN3 missense variant, absent from gnomAD/ExAC, reported by ClinVar as Uncertain Significance and never reported in the CAPN3-related-disease literature. Individual in-silico tools (SIFT: Tolerated, PolyPhen-2: Benign, Align-GVGD: Class C0) all lean benign, and the substituted residue is conserved as leucine in other mammals -- but deliberately NOT converted into a ComputationalEvidence record here: this project's PP3/BP4 model expects a single calibrated ensemble score (e.g. REVEL), not raw individual-tool outputs stacked together, which is exactly the kind of multi-tool-vote pattern the design guide warns against (see computational_evidence.py docstring). specification.version: ClinGen LGMD VCEP Specifications to the ACMG/AMP Guidelines for CAPN3, v2.0 (2025-07-09; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21434844)

cases.notes: Real ClinVar entry (VCV001453744 / RCV002002571), reported Pathogenic (last evaluated 2023-10-06, criteria provided/single submitter). GRCh38 chr15:42359806 A>G, NM_000070.3:c.1A>G, disrupting CAPN3's initiator Met codon directly (ClinVar molecular consequence: missense_variant + initiator_codon_variant). Coordinates independently confirmed via NCBI eutils esummary (canonical_spdi NC_000015.10:42359805:A:G), not just taken from a search snippet. gnomAD reported two slightly different exome AF figures in the ClinVar record (0.00001 and 0.00000, likely different gnomAD releases/subsets aggregated by ClinVar); the higher, more conservative value is used here. No ancestry-specific breakdown was available from this summary, so ancestry_specific_max_af is left unset (not the same as 'checked and found absent'). This is the project's first real start-loss (initiator codon) fixture -- PVS1's third documented scope gap, alongside the two splice-site fixtures (CAPN3_c.946-1G>A, CAPN3_c.2050+1G>A): the evaluator declines to auto-resolve start-loss variants because doing so correctly requires checking for a plausible downstream alternative in-frame start codon, which this project does not model (see pvs1.py, 'PVS1 scope'). Real ClinGen LGMD VCEP CAPN3 PVS1 flowchart likely does resolve this branch; this project's PVS1 evaluator does not implement that flowchart. UPDATED in batch 27: the alternative-start-codon question this fixture's original notes flagged as unresolved is now independently answered from real, primary sequence data. NM_000070.3's CDS (fetched directly from Ensembl's REST API for the matching canonical transcript ENST00000397163 -- confirmed as the same transcript by its CDS translation-start genomic coordinate, 42359806, matching this variant's own position exactly) is 2466 nt / 821 codons; scanning downstream in-frame codons finds the first alternative ATG at codon 228 (p.Met228), meaning re-initiation there would lose the first 227 residues -- 227/821 = 27.6% of the full-length protein, independently computed from the primary sequence, not estimated. That exceeds the ACGS 2024 / Abou Tayoun et al. 2018 decision tree's >10%-of-protein threshold for the automatic PVS1_Supporting downgrade on its own. It is also independently corroborated by this project's own curated fixture set: CAPN3_c.550del (p.Thr184fs, real, ClinVar Pathogenic) falls at residue 184, squarely within the region (residues 1-227) that would be lost if translation restarted at Met228 -- direct, real evidence that this N-terminal region is not merely dispensable padding, satisfying the rule's other disqualifying factor ('are there any reported pathogenic variants upstream of the potential initiation codon') independently of the percentage figure. Both factors point the same way, so PVS1 now returns MANUAL_REVIEW with a rationale citing exactly why (not the old generic 'not implemented' message) -- still not resolved to MET or NOT_MET, since the real protein-domain-criticality judgment call this evaluator declines to model would be needed to go further, but now grounded in real, independently-derived, dual-corroborated evidence rather than an unmodeled gap.

computational_evidence.calibration_source: ClinGen LGMD VCEP specification for CAPN3: REVEL >=0.70 for PP3 (Supporting)

cases.notes: Real ClinVar entry (VCV000468648 / ClinGen Allele Registry CA7511744), classified Pathogenic by the ClinGen LGMD VCEP itself (Evidence Repository record 7f534c0d-0dbe-4d2e-88e2-88c804cde635, approved 2025-04-22): erepo.clinicalgenome.org/evrepo/ui/interpretation/7f534c0d-0dbe-4d2e-88e2-88c804cde635. This is the project's first fixture sourced directly from an official VCEP expert curation record, not just a ClinVar aggregate classification -- and the first REAL calibrated computational (REVEL) score used anywhere in this project (closing a gap open since Milestone 1): REVEL=0.966, well above the real VCEP's own PP3 threshold (>=0.70). Population data: gnomAD v2.1.1 total AF 0.000148 (42/282854, all populations); gnomAD v4.1.0 exomes East Asian filtering allele frequency 0.001250-0.001929 (95% CI bounds, 62/39700 East Asian chromosomes) -- used here as ancestry_specific_max_af (upper bound, consistent with the FAF convention already used for PM2/BA1/BS1 in this project). NOTABLE: the real VCEP's own curation explicitly found this variant's East Asian FAF (0.001929) technically crosses their BS1 threshold (>0.001), but chose NOT to apply BS1 -- an explicit 'BS1 exception' -- because this is one of the most commonly reported CAPN3 variants in East Asian LGMD patients (i.e. a real, expert-judged founder-pathogenic-variant scenario, not a benign-common-variant one). This project's BS1 evaluator cannot make that judgment call (it has no access to case-count/segregation context), but it does correctly decline to auto-resolve: with overall_af below the BS1 threshold but ancestry_specific_max_af crossing it, the evaluator's existing founder-enrichment branch returns MANUAL_REVIEW rather than silently applying BS1 -- landing on exactly the same 'a human needs to look at this' conclusion the real VCEP reached, for the same underlying reason, without knowing why. The real variant's actual Pathogenic classification rests almost entirely on criteria this project's 6-criterion engine does not implement at all (PM3_Strong: observed in trans with a pathogenic variant across multiple case reports; PP1_Strong: segregation in 6 affected relatives across 4 families; PP4: phenotype + reduced calpain-3 protein expression) -- PM2 is explicitly NOT_MET in the real curation too (too common in East Asian populations for PM2_Supporting's <0.0001 threshold), and PP3 (REVEL) is the ONLY real criterion this project's engine and the real VCEP curation share. cases.notes:
Real ClinVar entry (Variation ID 553852; dbSNP rs746075428), official HGVS NM_000070.3(CAPN3):c.1395GGA[2] (p.Glu467del), equivalently written c.1401_1403del. Reviewed by expert panel (ClinGen LGMD VCEP, evaluated 2025-06-24): Pathogenic, via PM3_Very Strong + PP4_Moderate + PM2_Supporting + PM4 (none of which besides PM2/PM4 are implemented by this project). Sourced specifically as batch 14's real fixture for the newly-implemented PM4 evaluator, closing the loop on a variant this project's own notes had referenced by name (in the CAPN3_c.2257G>A enrichment write-up) without ever formally sourcing it. 

repeat_region curation note (the reason this fixture was chosen deliberately, not casually): the official HGVS uses short-tandem-repeat notation, c.1395GGA[2] -- the reference allele is a GGA-trinucleotide run (GGAGGAGGA, 3 copies) and this variant contracts it to 2 copies (GGAGGA), deleting one GGA unit and one glutamate residue. Read naively, that looks exactly like the kind of 'repeat region' PM4 is defined to exclude (Richards et al. 2015: '...in a nonrepeat region'). But the real ClinGen LGMD VCEP's own Pathogenic classification for this exact variant applies PM4 anyway, with no repeat-region caveat or discussion in their comment -- they simply state '...is expected to cause an in-frame deletion of one amino acid, p.(Glu467del) (PM4).' Taken at face value, that is a real, expert-panel-level judgment that a small (2-3 copy) incidental trinucleotide run inside an otherwise unremarkable coding region is not the kind of 'repeat region' the PM4 exclusion is aimed at -- unlike, say, a polyglutamine/polyalanine tract or a locus with a documented high population rate of benign in-frame indels, which is what the exclusion exists to guard against (indels there are common, expected, and usually uninformative; sequencing/alignment artifacts are also more likely). This fixture's repeat_region is therefore curated as false, on the strength of that real-world precedent, not guessed either way. 

protein_length_change_aa is curated as 1 (a single glutamate residue), which is what the VCEP, Invitae/Labcorp, and LabCorp submitter comments all independently confirm ('deletion of 1 amino acid(s)', 'remove one amino acid'). This project's PM4 evaluator downgrades single-residue in-frame changes to Supporting strength by default (the general ClinGen SVI caution, not CAPN3-specific). Worth flagging honestly: the real VCEP's comment states plain 'PM4' with no strength qualifier, unlike their explicitly qualified 'PM3_Very Strong', 'PP4_Moderate', and 'PM2_Supporting' in the same sentence -- which reads as their having applied PM4 at its unmodified default (Moderate), not Supporting. This project's generic Supporting default for this fixture is therefore a disclosed departure from what the real CAPN3-specific VCEP appears to have done, not a hidden one -- consistent with how this project has already handled other real-vs-project strength mismatches (e.g. PM2's Supporting-vs-Moderate story elsewhere in this file). 

Population frequency: gnomAD v4.1.0 exomes (matching the VCEP's own primary source), overall AF 1.437e-05 (21/1,461,872 total alleles), NFE-specific 1.888e-05 (21/1,111,998), both retrieved directly from Ensembl's variation endpoint (dbSNP rs746075428 population frequencies) rather than approximated from the VCEP's filtering-allele-frequency (FAF) statistic, which is a more conservative upper-confidence-bound figure, not a raw allele frequency, and would not be a fair like-for-like match to how this project reports overall_af / ancestry_specific_max_af elsewhere. Both figures sit far below CAPN3's real ClinGen LGMD VCEP thresholds (PM2_Supporting <0.0001; BS1_Strong >0.001; BA1 >0.003). Exact GRCh38 coordinates were not independently re-verified during curation beyond the ClinVar-stated 42401681-42401683 (see variant.coordinate_verified=false, matching this project's existing convention for HGVS/ClinVar-ID-anchored fixtures).

PS1 Strong (4) + PM2 Supporting (1, ABSENT from gnomAD) + PP3 Supporting (1, synthetic REVEL 0.9) clears Table 5's '1 Strong + >=2 Supporting' Likely Pathogenic rule -- chosen specifically to give PS1 a clean, complete classification-tier demonstration rather than only an isolated MET result.

cases.notes: SYNTHETIC fixture, built deliberately (not sourced from ClinVar) to exercise batch 26's new PVS1 splice-RNA-evidence MET/Very-Strong path end-to-end, modeled on a minigene/RT-PCR splicing assay: splicing_rna_evidence=CONFIRMED_NULL_EQUIVALENT represents a hypothetical assay result showing complete loss of the normal transcript and exclusive production of an out-of-frame exon-skipped product predicted to trigger nonsense-mediated decay -- the clean, unambiguous case this branch is built for. population_evidence is deliberately NOT_ASSESSED (not ABSENT) so this fixture's PVS1 MET result stands alone as a single contributing criterion (both Table 5 and the Bayesian point system cap a single criterion at VUS regardless of its own strength) -- keeping this fixture focused purely on demonstrating the new PVS1 branch, without also becoming an incidental new Table-5-vs-Bayesian divergence case (already well covered by real fixtures elsewhere, see README's Milestone 5 design note). A real CAPN3/DMD splice variant with this level of experimental precision (a stated frame/NMD outcome, not just 'disrupts splicing') was searched for during this batch's research but not found in the available (non-blocked) sources -- the three real curated splice fixtures (CAPN3_c.946-1G>A, CAPN3_c.2050+1G>A, DMD_c.93+1G>A) all remain at PVS1 MANUAL_REVIEW; see their own notes for exactly what evidence each has and why it falls short of this bar. Disclosed as an open real-data gap, same 'searched, not found, still open' treatment given to other gaps in this project (e.g. PS1's same-nucleotide precedent pair, BS3's clean MET example).

cases.notes: SYNTHETIC fixture, built deliberately (not sourced from ClinVar) to exercise batch 27's new 'no alternative start codon identified' PVS1 MET/Very-Strong path end-to-end: alternative_start_codon_identified=False represents a hypothetical case where no downstream in-frame ATG exists at all (unlike the real CAPN3_c.1A>G fixture, which does have one, at codon 228) -- per the ACGS 2024 / Abou Tayoun et al. 2018 rule, 'If no alternative in-frame start codon is identified, use PVS1 at maximum strength.' No real CAPN3/DMD start-loss variant with a CONFIRMED absence of any downstream in-frame start codon was identified during this batch's research (CAPN3's own real fixture does have one); constructing this case synthetically instead, same 'searched, not found, still open, demonstrate on a labeled synthetic instead' treatment used for PS1's MET path (batch 22) and the PVS1 splice-RNA-evidence MET path (batch 26). population_evidence is deliberately NOT_ASSESSED (not ABSENT) so PVS1 MET stands as this fixture's only contributing criterion -- both Table 5 and the Bayesian point system cap a single criterion at VUS regardless of its own strength (the 2-criterion minimum rule), keeping this fixture focused on demonstrating the new PVS1 branch alone rather than incidentally becoming another Table-5-vs-Bayesian divergence case, same discipline as CAPN3_SYNTH_PVS1_SPLICE_RNA_01 (batch 26).

cases.notes: SYNTHETIC fixture, built deliberately (not sourced from ClinVar) to exercise batch 27's new automatic-downgrade PVS1 MET/Supporting path end-to-end: alternative_start_codon_identified=True, alternative_start_codon_percent_protein_lost=4.0 (<=10%), alternative_start_codon_preceded_by_pathogenic_variant=False -- the clean case the ACGS 2024 / Abou Tayoun et al. 2018 rule's automatic downgrade is built for ('the only null variant that should be applied the downgraded criteria PVS1_Supporting is a variant of initiation codon when a new methionine is not preceded by a pathogenic variant'). CAPN3's own real start-loss fixture (CAPN3_c.1A>G) does not qualify for this branch -- its alternative start codon is at 27.6% of the protein, well above the 10% threshold, and is preceded by a real pathogenic variant (CAPN3_c.550del) -- so no real CAPN3/DMD fixture was available to demonstrate this specific branch; constructing it synthetically instead, same treatment as CAPN3_SYNTH_PVS1_STARTLOSS_NO_ALT_01 above.
